items.title: Section: Chapter Sixteen Opens — Veneration, Association, and the Immeasurables

items.zh: 云何菩薩供養、親近、修習無量？嗢拕南曰：供三寶、親善友、修無量最為後。
items.en: From the Bodhisattva Stage within the Basic Section, the chapter on the initial yoga foundation, chapter sixteen: veneration, association, and the immeasurables. How does a bodhisattva who has generated the supreme mind of awakening properly venerate and make offerings to the three jewels, approach and rely on genuine spiritual friends, and cultivate the immeasurable states of loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity? A summary verse states: "Venerating the three jewels; approaching good friends; cultivating the immeasurables, placed last of all." The verse first names its topic in outline — three great sections: venerating the three jewels, approaching good friends, and, placed deliberately last, cultivating the four immeasurables.

items.title: Section: The Ten Kinds of Veneration Named

items.zh: 云何菩薩於如來所供養如來？當知供養略有十種。一、設利羅供養、二、制多供養，三、現前供養，四、不現前供養，五、自作供養，六、教他供養，七、財敬供養，八、廣大供養，九、無染供養，十、正行供養。
items.en: How does a bodhisattva venerate the Tathāgata in the Tathāgata's own presence? One should understand that veneration is, in brief, of ten kinds: first, relic veneration; second, stupa veneration; third, present veneration; fourth, absent veneration; fifth, self-performed veneration; sixth, teaching-others veneration; seventh, wealth-and-respect veneration; eighth, vast veneration; ninth, undefiled veneration; tenth, proper-practice veneration.

items.title: Section: Relic Veneration and Stupa Veneration — Honouring the Buddha's Body, and Every Structure Built to Hold It

items.zh: 若諸菩薩，親現供養如來色身，是名設利羅供養。若諸菩薩，於為如來所造一切若窣堵波、若龕、若臺、若故制多、新制多所設諸供養，是名制多供養。
items.en: Bodhisattvas who directly and personally venerate the Tathāgata's own physical body — this is called relic veneration. Whatever veneration bodhisattvas offer at any reliquary mound, niche, platform, old shrine, or new shrine built for the Tathāgata's sake — this is called stupa veneration.

items.title: Section: Present Veneration — One Buddha's Dharma-Nature Is Every Buddha's Own

items.zh: 若諸菩薩，於如來身、或制多所親面對前，現矚現見而設供養，是名現前供養。若諸菩薩，於如來所、若制多所，現前施設供養具時，發起增上意樂俱心、淨信俱心，作是思惟：若一如來法性，即是去來今世一切如來法性；若一如來制多法性，即是十方無邊無際一切世界所有如來制多法性。是故我今供現如來，即是供養其餘三世一切如來；供現制多，即是供養其餘十方無邊無際一切世界若窣堵波、若龕、若臺、若故制多、若新制多。當知是名菩薩俱供現不現前一切如來及以制多。
items.en: Bodhisattvas who set out veneration directly facing the Tathāgata's own body or a shrine, genuinely seen and beheld before their own eyes — this is called present veneration. When bodhisattvas set out veneration's own implements directly before the Tathāgata or a shrine, they raise a mind joined with heightened aspiration and a mind joined with pure faith, contemplating in this way: the true nature of this one Tathāgata is precisely the true nature of every Tathāgata across past, future, and present; the true nature of this one shrine is precisely the true nature of every shrine belonging to every Tathāgata across every world throughout the ten directions, boundless and without limit. Therefore, in venerating the Tathāgata now present before me, I venerate every other Tathāgata across the three times as well; in venerating this shrine now present, I venerate every other reliquary mound, niche, platform, old shrine, and new shrine across every boundless world in the ten directions as well. One should understand this to be called a bodhisattva jointly venerating every Tathāgata and every shrine, present and absent alike.

items.title: Section: Absent Veneration — Visualisation After the Buddha's Passing, and Boundless Merit From Raising Even a Single Image

items.zh: 若諸菩薩，於不現前一切如來及以制多作如來想，普為三世一切如來、一切十方如來制多施設供養，當知是名菩薩唯供不現前佛及以制多。若諸菩薩，佛涅槃後，為如來故造立形像，若窣堵波、若龕、若臺，隨力隨能或一或二，或復眾多，乃至百千俱胝等數；如是菩薩於如來所，設不現前弘廣供養，當獲無量大福德果，攝受無量廣大梵福。菩薩由此，能於無量劫大劫中，不墮惡趣。由是因緣，非不圓滿無上正等菩提資糧。
items.en: Bodhisattvas who form the thought "this is the Tathāgata" towards every Tathāgata and shrine not presently before them, thereby setting out veneration universally towards every Tathāgata across the three times and every shrine throughout the ten directions — one should understand this to be called a bodhisattva venerating only the absent buddhas and shrines. After the Buddha's parinirvāṇa, bodhisattvas who, for the Tathāgata's sake, build images, or reliquary mounds, or niches, or platforms, whether one or two according to their own strength and ability, or a great many, even reaching hundreds of thousands or millions in number — such bodhisattvas, by setting out this vast, absent veneration in the Tathāgata's presence, will obtain the fruit of immeasurable, great merit and virtue, gathering in immeasurable, vast Brahmā-realm blessing. Through this cause, bodhisattvas are able, across immeasurable eons of great eons, to avoid falling into the lower realms. Through this very cause and condition, their requisite provisions for supreme, complete awakening are by no means left unfulfilled.

items.title: Section: Present, Absent, or Both — Ranking the Karmic Fruit; Then Self-Performed and Teaching-Others Veneration

items.zh: 此中菩薩，唯供現前佛及制多，應知獲得廣大福果。若唯供養不現前佛及以制多，應知獲得大大福果。若俱供養現不現前佛及制多，應知獲得最大福果，為無有上。若諸菩薩，於如來所、若制多所欲設供養，唯自手作，不使奴婢、作使、朋友、僚庶、親屬，不依懈惰諸放逸處而設供養，是名菩薩自作供養。若諸菩薩，
items.en: Among these, bodhisattvas who venerate only present buddhas and shrines should be understood to obtain a vast fruit of merit. Those who venerate only absent buddhas and shrines should be understood to obtain a greater, still vaster fruit. Those who venerate both present and absent buddhas and shrines together should be understood to obtain the single greatest fruit, unsurpassed by any other. Bodhisattvas who, wishing to set out veneration in the Tathāgata's presence or at a shrine, do so entirely with their own hands, without employing servants, hired hands, friends, retainers, or relatives, and without any trace of laziness or heedlessness in setting it out — this is called a bodhisattva's self-performed veneration. Bodhisattvas who presently have only a small amount of offerable wealth, and who, moved by a compassionate mind, deliberately give it to suffering beings of little merit and little means so that they may use it to venerate the Tathāgata or a shrine, wishing them much future happiness as a result — when such beings receive this gift and venerate the Tathāgata and the shrine with it, while the bodhisattva themselves offers nothing directly — one should understand this to be called a bodhisattva's veneration solely through teaching others.

items.title: Section: Rallying an Entire Community to Venerate Together — From King and Brahmin Down to the Lowest Outcaste

items.zh: 於如來所、若制多所欲設供養，非唯自作，亦勸父母、妻子、奴婢、作使、朋友、僚庶、親屬，及他國王、王子、大臣、長者、居士、若婆羅門、國邑聚落饒財商主，下至一切男女大小、貧匱苦厄旃荼羅等，及以親教、軌範諸師，共住、近住一切弟子，同梵行者、諸出家者、外道等眾，令於如來、若制多所，隨力隨能作諸供養，當知是名菩薩自他咸共供養。若諸菩薩，現有少分可供財物，興悲愍心，故思施與貧苦少福無力有情，令於如來、若制多所持用供養，願彼當來多受安樂。彼得此物，供養如來及以制多，菩薩於斯自無所供，當知是名菩薩唯教他設供養。此中菩薩，若唯自供佛及制多，應知獲得廣大福果。若唯教他，應知獲得大大福果。若能自他俱共供養，應知獲得最大福果，為無有上。
items.en: Bodhisattvas who, wishing to set out veneration in the Tathāgata's presence or at a shrine, do so not only themselves but also urge their parents, spouse, servants, hired hands, friends, retainers, and relatives, as well as other kings, princes, ministers, elders, householders, brahmins, and wealthy merchants of the country's cities and villages, down to every man and woman, old and young, and even the destitute, suffering, and outcaste, together with their own preceptors and instructing teachers, fellow disciples living together or nearby, companions in the pure conduct, monastics, and even followers of other paths, to make whatever veneration each one's own strength and ability allows in the Tathāgata's presence or at a shrine — one should understand this to be called a bodhisattva's veneration jointly performed by self and others together. Among these, bodhisattvas who venerate the Buddha and the shrine only by themselves should be understood to obtain a vast fruit of merit. Those who only teach others to venerate should be understood to obtain a greater fruit. Those able to venerate jointly, both by themselves and through others, should be understood to obtain the single greatest fruit, unsurpassed by any other.

blocks.text: Fascicle 44 opens a new chapter on **veneration, relying on spiritual friends, and the immeasurables** (供養親近無量品), then begins the chapter on the **factors of awakening** (菩提分品). Today: ten ways of honouring the Buddha.

"How does a bodhisattva venerate the Three Jewels, approach good friends, and cultivate the immeasurables?" Master Cháng Bǎi explains the title "Tathāgata": ultimate truth is "thus", right awakening is "come".
Veneration of relics (the Buddha's body); of stupas; present; absent; done oneself; done by encouraging others; with wealth and respect; vast; undefiled; and by right practice.
Venerating the Buddha in person (Venerable Miào Jìng: śarīra means "body"). A stupa holds relics; a caitya marks a place: birth, awakening, first teaching (Master Cháng Bǎi).

Before the Buddha or a shrine. "The Dharma nature of one Tathāgata is the Dharma nature of all Tathāgatas past, future, and present; so venerating this one is venerating all." Venerable Miào Jìng: the "pure faith" involved is really wisdom.
Thinking "this is the Tathāgata" towards all Buddhas and shrines not present. Making even one image brings "immeasurable merit"; Venerable Miào Jìng: the merit of the Brahmā heaven.

Present only is vast; absent only, greater; both, the greatest. Likewise doing it oneself, encouraging others, or both. One urges "parents, spouse, servants, friends, relatives", from kings to the lowest. Master Cháng Bǎi: doing good oneself and urging others is best.

quiz.q: According to this chapter's summary verse, what three things does a bodhisattva do?
options: venerate the three jewels, approach good friends, cultivate the immeasurables
quiz.why: "How does a bodhisattva venerate, approach, and cultivate the immeasurables? The summary verse: venerate the three jewels, approach good friends, cultivate the immeasurables last." Master Cháng Bǎi: first veneration, second good friends, third the four immeasurables.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain "Tathāgata" in "venerating the Tathāgata"?
options: ultimate truth is "thus," right awakening is "come" — the reward body; coming by the true path to awaken — the response body
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: ultimate truth is "thus," right awakening is "come" — this is the Tathāgata as reward body; coming by the path of reality to accomplish right awakening — the Tathāgata as response body.

quiz.q: "Directly venerating the Tathāgata's physical body is called śarīra veneration." How do the two lectures explain "śarīra"?
options: Miào Jìng: it means "body" — here the Buddha present, veneration before him; Cháng Bǎi: formerly "relics," here the Tathāgata's physical body
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: śarīra is "body" — here the Buddha present, venerated in person. Master Cháng Bǎi: formerly translated "relics," here it refers to the Tathāgata's physical body.

quiz.q: On stupa veneration, how does Master Cháng Bǎi distinguish "stūpa" and "caitya"?
options: a place with relics is a stūpa; without relics, a caitya
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: a place with relics is called a stūpa; without relics, a caitya — the Buddha's birthplace, awakening place, first teaching, and parinirvāṇa are the four caityas. Venerable Miào Jìng: stūpa means pagoda, also "high, conspicuous place."

quiz.q: Venerating a present Tathāgata, what does the bodhisattva reflect so the offering reaches all Tathāgatas?
options: one Tathāgata's dharma-nature is that of all Tathāgatas of the three times; venerating one is venerating all
quiz.why: "The dharma-nature of one Tathāgata is the dharma-nature of all Tathāgatas past, future, and present … so venerating this present Tathāgata is venerating all." Master Cháng Bǎi: buddhas differ in causal conditions but are equal in dharma-body qualities.

quiz.q: How do the fruits compare for venerating present, absent, or both? What does each lecture stress?
options: treatise: present vast, absent greater, both greatest; Cháng Bǎi: practising both brings the greatest fruit; Miào Jìng: the size depends on sincere, doubt-free faith
quiz.why: Present only — vast; absent only — greater still; both — the greatest, unsurpassed. Master Cháng Bǎi: practising both brings the greatest fruit. Venerable Miào Jìng: if your faith is especially sincere and doubt-free, the merit is great.

quiz.q: Among self-performed, only teaching others, and both together, which brings the greatest fruit?
options: both self and others together — the greatest, unsurpassed
quiz.why: Self only — vast; others only — greater; both — the greatest, unsurpassed. Master Cháng Bǎi: doing good oneself and urging others too — benefiting self and others — is most complete.
